To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the relative activation times (phase angles) of cell-cycling gene expressions are coherent across experiments; (b) there is an association between the relative activation times for the same gene under different experimental conditions; and (c) the relative activation time for the same gene in the same experiment is not associated with the relative activation time of another gene in the same experimental condition.

the circular regression model is an appropriate model for analyzing the association and coherence between two sets of gene expression data and the circular regression model can be used to identify genes that are coherent across experiments.
we propose a circular-circular model to assess the association and coherence between two cell-cycle experiments and apply the proposed method to a HeLa data set to illustrate the methodology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a geometric approach to analyze cell-cycling gene expressions across multiple cell-cycle experiments, which is a novel application of circular statistics to the analysis of cell-cycle data.
the development of a new statistical approach for the analysis of cell-cycle gene-expression experiments.
developing a statistical methodology for analyzing cell-cycling gene-expression data from multiple experiments simultaneously.

our proposed methodology provides a powerful tool to study the coherence and association of genes across different experimental conditions.
the genes studied are associated and coherent under different experimental conditions.
the genes are not only associated but also coherent across experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methodology is useful in analyzing gene-expression data from cell-cycle studies, and it can help identify genes that are associated and coherent under different experimental conditions.
we have provided a statistical methodology to determine association and the extent of coherence of cell-cycle genes under different experimental situations.

we provide a novel statistical approach to determine the association of the relative activation time of genes under different experimental condition and to assess the coherence of genes across multiple experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed methodology can be used to assess the coherence and association of the relative activation phases of cell-cycling gene expression under varying experimental conditions, and thus, it may provide useful insight into how the cell cycle is regulated under different experimental conditions.
our proposed methodology can be applied to a wide range of cell-cycle experiments to study coherence across experiments, which is not possible using existing methodologies.

it provides an appropriate statistical framework for the analysis of multiple cell-cycle experiments, which can be used to determine association and/or coherence of the activation patterns of cell-cycling gene across experiments.
